title: ARU/BS&T historical discovery and selected industrial interface

transport_capacity_events.description: A soft and uneven U.S. freight market, high operating costs, financing pressure, and trade-policy uncertainty continued to pressure small and mid-sized carriers and encouraged network consolidation.
transport_capacity_events.capacity_effect: Context for counterparty concentration; no company-specific effect is inferred directly from the external evidence.

transport_capacity_events.description: A fictional combination among qualified regional transport providers reduces the number of carriers willing and able to serve the Red Wash lane.
The surviving carrier allocates less scheduling capacity to the low-frequency Red Wash uranium lane.
transport_capacity_events.capacity_effect: A planned delivery window must be rescheduled and the concentration risk becomes operationally visible.

transport_capacity_events.description: Red Wash opens a replacement/additional-qualified-carrier search; operating analysis later broadens the question to rail access and a more resilient transportation alternative.
transport_capacity_events.capacity_effect: The search begins with carrier continuity rather than a predetermined railroad acquisition.

transport_capacity_events.description: Route and interface mapping identifies a nearby line and prompts the operating question 'Whose line is this?'; the inquiry surfaces ARU and BS&T.
transport_capacity_events.capacity_effect: ARU is surfaced through operating analysis before November-December diligence and January 7, 2026 close; no 2025 Red Wash service.

shipment_schedule_exceptions.revised_window: revised qualified-carrier slot inside the 2025 annual delivery period
shipment_schedule_exceptions.outcome: Delivery completed; no lost annual sales and no change to 2025 annual revenue.

carrier_market_scan.finding: Qualified but capacity-constrained after the synthetic consolidation event.
Potential redundancy requires capacity, insurance, route, security, and uranium-specific qualification diligence.
A mixed qualified-carrier, truck, transload, and rail model may improve resilience if all gates are proved.
